summary: Hero episode on Uruguay's Tupamaros, Robin Hood-style urban guerrillas of the 1960s and 70s, and member José Mujica, who survived 14 years in the dictatorship's prisons and was elected president in 2009.

evidence.note: Batlle-era welfare state background from 1903; treated as context, not story
Sendic organises cane cutters and founds the movement in 1963
bank robberies and armed propaganda escalate 1963-1968
Mujica born 1935 to a poor farming family near Montevideo
kidnapping of US adviser Mitrione, said to teach torture, in 1970
US military aid and CIA backing for the Uruguayan government
Frente Amplio and the 1971 election before the dictatorship
Mujica's solitary confinement in army prisons, about 14 years
1985 return to democracy and amnesty frees the prisoners
2009 election; presidency legalises gay marriage, marijuana, abortion
present-day state of the movement under a conservative government

notes: Title names the Tupamaros, descriptions name Mujica, so both are primary. A long opening segment on Batlle's early-1900s reforms and the 1950s economic collapse is treated as background, so covered_span starts at Mujica's birth. Mujica was alive at release (died 2025), so covered_span ends 2021. Primary theme terrorism vs coups-insurrections is a judgment call; no theme for a positive hero insurgency.
